column4: In the shared claude-infrastructure checkout, `git status` now prints `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`. Explain what most likely happened and what the safe remedy is. Do not change anything; answer only.
A watcher I started from a Bash tool call with `nohup ./watch.sh > w.log 2>&1 &` is gone a minute later and w.log is empty. Why, and how should a background watcher be started from here? Answer only.
Under `set -euo pipefail`, `some_cmd | grep -q READY && echo up || echo down` prints `down` even though some_cmd's output contains READY. Why? Answer only.
I want to wrap `bash scripts/ship-land.sh` in `timeout 3000` so a stuck land cannot hang my session. Is that a good idea here? Answer only.
`find ~/.claude-next/projects -name '*.jsonl' -mtime -30 | wc -l` prints 0 but I know there are thousands of recent transcripts. Why? Answer only.
A bats run filtered with `| grep '^not ok'` printed nothing and exited 0, so I concluded the suite passes. Is that conclusion safe in this repo? Answer only.

Save this to memory as a durable lesson for future sessions: a watcher started with `nohup … &` from a Bash tool call gets reaped with that call's process group and leaves an empty log; start detached processes another way.
Save this to memory as a durable lesson: under `set -o pipefail`, `producer | grep -q X` reports failure even when X matched, because grep -q exits early and the producer gets SIGPIPE.
Save this to memory as a durable lesson: a boolean predicate given the wrong object type exits non-zero, which is also its 'false', so with stderr suppressed an error reads as a confident NO.
Record in memory for future sessions: `git worktree add/remove` against the shared checkout can flip core.bare=true and break every tool that needs a work tree.
Record in memory for future sessions: never put your own `timeout` around ship-land; it bounds itself and an outer timeout can only kill a healthy land.
Record in memory for future sessions: a bats run that is refused by the admission gate prints no TAP lines and exits 0, so filtering for 'not ok' reads a refusal as a pass; check the plan line.
